corrector

Source: README.en.md

Versión en español

An R package for grading R programming exercises. Each student hands in one file per exercise (.R, .Rmd or .qmd), the teacher writes the tests, and corrector grades the whole class at once, on your computer. It reads the submissions of a Moodle assignment and prepares the feedback to upload back.

Guides: Grading pipeline · Cheat-resistant grading · Function reference

Installation

# install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("anevolbap/corrector")

Minimal end-to-end example

library(corrector)

# --- 1. Create a fake submission folder ---
dir.create("submissions/garcia", recursive = TRUE)
dir.create("submissions/lopez",  recursive = TRUE)
dir.create("tests")

writeLines(
  'ceros_cuadratica <- function(a, b, c) {
     d <- b^2 - 4*a*c
     c((-b - sqrt(d)) / (2*a), (-b + sqrt(d)) / (2*a))
   }',
  "submissions/garcia/ejercicio1.R"
)

writeLines(
  'ceros_cuadratica <- function(a, b, c) c(0, 0)',  # wrong
  "submissions/lopez/ejercicio1.R"
)

writeLines(
  'test_ejercicio1_raices <- function() {
     all(ceros_cuadratica(1, 0, -1) == c(-1, 1))
   }
   test_ejercicio1_tipo <- function() {
     is.numeric(ceros_cuadratica(1, 0, -1))
   }',
  "tests/test_ejercicio1.R"
)

# --- 2. Grade ---
results <- grade_submissions("submissions/", test_dir = "tests/")
results
# <grade_results> 4 rows, 2 students, 1 exercises
# Status:
#   pass          3
#   fail          1

# --- 3. Summarise and export ---
grade_report(results)
export_to_html(results, "report.html")
export_to_csv(results,  "grades.csv")

Submissions and tests

One folder per student and one test file per exercise. The test file name must match the exercise:

submissions/
├── garcia_juan/
│   ├── ejercicio1.R
│   └── ejercicio2.Rmd
└── lopez_maria/
    └── ejercicio1.R

tests/
├── test_ejercicio1.R
└── test_ejercicio2.R

A test file holds functions named test_<exercise>_<case> that return TRUE or FALSE. They can also use testthat expectations (expect_equal() and others).

# tests/test_ejercicio1.R
test_ejercicio1_roots <- function() {
  all(ceros_cuadratica(1, 0, -1) == c(-1, 1))
}
  • The expected exercises come from the test folder. An exercise the student did not hand in is recorded as missing, not skipped.
  • File names are matched ignoring case: Ejercicio1.R counts as ejercicio1. For .Rmd and .qmd, the R chunks run.
  • Submissions can come as a folder or a .zip. Each student’s name comes from their folder (garcia_juan becomes Garcia); change it with student_name_fn.
  • For Moodle, pass the .zip from “Download all submissions” with layout = "moodle". It works with and without “Download submissions in folders”.
results <- grade_submissions("assignment1-submissions.zip", test_dir = "tests/",
                             layout = "moodle")

What else it does

  • Grades: student_scores() gives partial credit and takes weights per test or per exercise; grade_scale() turns that score into a 1-10 grade.
  • Feedback: export_feedback() writes one file per student, in Spanish or English; export_moodle_feedback() packs them in a .zip to upload to Moodle.
  • Summaries and export: grade_report(), plot_report(), export_to_csv(), export_to_html() and export_to_sheets().
  • Similar submissions: compare_submissions() looks for copies, even after renaming variables or changing spacing or comments.
  • Time limit and speed: each test gets timeout seconds (default 10), and workers grades several students at once.
  • To try it: example_results() returns sample results, and system.file("examples", package = "corrector") holds tests for five exercises.

All of this, with examples, in the Grading pipeline guide.

Security and cheating

corrector is not a sandbox: with the default engine, callr, student code runs as your user and can read and write your files. It blocks the common tricks (redefining all(), == or comparison methods) and notes suspicious code, which grade_report() lists for you to check by hand.

  • engine = "isolated" runs the student code in another process, so tricks such as attach() do not change the grade.
  • engine = "container" does the same inside Docker, with no network and only the exercise’s files, so the code cannot reach your computer either.
results <- grade_submissions("submissions/", test_dir = "tests/",
                             engine = "container", workers = 4)

How to pick an engine, build the Docker image, and write tests that are hard to fool: Cheat-resistant grading.

Alternatives

corrector is for exercises that students write as files on their own computer and that the teacher grades afterwards, all at once, with their own tests, with no server and no student accounts. Other R packages cover other cases:

  • gradethis: checks code exercise by exercise inside an interactive learnr tutorial, with instant feedback. The exercise lives inside the tutorial and needs a Shiny server.
  • exams: generates random questions and exports them to Moodle, Canvas, PDF and more. It grades answers (a number, a choice, a text), not the code the student wrote.
  • RTutor: interactive problem sets with automatic checking and progress tracking, in its own format.

corrector is not interactive: students do not see results while they write, unless you give them the tests to run.
